items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: Cliff Gross... who had been with us earlier... I would still play radio programs in the afternoon and side dates with members of the band

ctx.x: I really, I feel painfully ignorant of certain of the things that were happening in Western Swing. And, uh, uh, that's why a lot of things are lacking, you know, in this, but that's why

I'm here. Did you ever hear the name Cliff Gross, the hillbilly violinist Cliff Gross, who came from Kentucky, who had been with us earlier. But even while I was with the Dubois, in the 1937 to 40, I kept hanging around there, you got to stretch that 40 to around 42, because I would still play radio programs in the afternoon and side dates with members of the band, and records with Boyd. But during that period of time, the format changed a great deal as the hillbilly musicians became swing conscious, and as that…
You were trying for more elaborate arrangements. And then we found out who were you imitating or trying to come up to.
